saa-med-025.text: An organisation needs to ensure that the audit records of the CloudTrail of all accounts are collected centrally and any adulteration in the log files delivered can be detected. Which two settings meet these requirements?
options: Configure CloudTrail manually in each account and send the logs by weekly email
Store logs in the Audit Forum Store
Replace CloudTrail by VPC Centralized Flow Logs
Create an organization trail (organization trail) delivering in a central pocket and enable log file integrity validation
saa-med-025.explanation: The trail organisation applies the CloudTrail automatically to all member accounts with centralized delivery, and integrity validation generates signed digest files that allow you to verify if the logs have been changed.
saa-med-025.hint: An 'organization trail' resolves the collection; the signed 'digest' files resolve the evidence of adultery.
optionRationales: The trail organisation applies the CloudTrail automatically to all member accounts with centralized delivery, and integrity validation generates signed digest files that allow you to verify if the logs have been changed.
Manual configuration per account is fragile and divergent, and e-mail is neither centralized collection nor integrity proof mechanism.
Flow Logs record network traffic, not calls from API Administrative requirements in audits.
The Forum Store is ephemeral — audit logs would disappear with instances, violating retention and integrity requirements.

saa-med-026.text: A ticket site suffers from bots that make thousands of requests per minute from few IP addresses, exhausting the virtual stock. The team wants to automatically limit customers who exceed a volume of requests in 5 minutes, temporarily blocking them. AWS WAF implements this control?
options: AWS Shield Standard
Managed Rules of SQL injection
Rate-based rules, which block IPs that exceed the time window requirement limit
Security Groups with connection limit
saa-med-026.explanation: Rate-based rules count IP requests in sliding windows and apply automatic lock to those above the threshold, mitigating bots and volumetric abuses in the layer 7.
saa-med-026.hint: The criterion for blocking is the VELOCIDADE of requests per customer — search for the rule 'based on fee'.
optionRationales: Rate-based rules count IP requests in sliding windows and apply automatic lock to those above the threshold, mitigating bots and volumetric abuses in the layer 7.
SQLi rules inspect injection patterns in content — do not limit volume of requests per customer.
The Shield Standard Mitigates Volumetric Layer Attacks 3/4 automatically, but does not apply IP fee limits on requests HTTP legitimate in the layer 7.
Security Groups allow or deny by port/origin — do not count or limit request rate HTTP.

saa-med-027.text: An architect will associate a certificate TLS of the AWS Certificate Manager to a distribution of the Amazon CloudFront. What regional requirement applies to this certificate?
options: The certificate must be in the same region as the original bucket
The certificate may be in any region, since the ACM is global
The CloudFront does not accept certificates from ACM, only manually imported certificates
The certificate shall be issued or imported into the ACM of the region us-east-1 (Northern Virginia)
saa-med-027.explanation: The CloudFront is a global service that seeks certificates exclusively in ACM Of us-east-1 — certificates in other regions do not appear for distribution association.
saa-med-027.hint: Global service, certificate safe in a specific region: the historical 'capital' of the AWS.
optionRationales: The CloudFront is a global service that seeks certificates exclusively in ACM Of us-east-1 — certificates in other regions do not appear for distribution association.
The Region of origin is irrelevant to the distribution certificate — the requirement is fixed in us-east-1.
The ACM is regional; for regional services (such as ALB) the local region is used, but the CloudFront requires us-east-1.
The CloudFront accepts certificates from ACM normally (free of charge and with automatic renewal) — provided that in us-east-1.

saa-med-028.text: By regulatory requirement, financial records recorded in S3 may not be altered or excluded by anyone — or even administrators — during the retention period of 7 years (model WORM: write once, read many). S3 imposes this immutability?
options: Move objects to S3 Deep Archive Glacier
Bucket policy denying exclusions
S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with defined retention period
Simple Bucket Version
saa-med-028.explanation: Object Lock in Compliance mode prevents any user-protected versions, including root, from being changed and deleted until the end of retention — the mechanism WORM native to S3 for regulatory requirements.
saa-med-028.hint: WORM real regulator requires 'object lock' in the way that the root can't unlock.
optionRationales: Object Lock in Compliance mode prevents any user-protected versions, including root, from being changed and deleted until the end of retention — the mechanism WORM native to S3 for regulatory requirements.
Version preserves versions, but users with permission can still permanently exclude them — there is no guaranteed immutability.
Policies can be changed by administrators at any time — do not guarantee the required immutability against administrators themselves.
Archiving classes reduce cost, but objects can still be excluded by those who have permission.

saa-med-029.text: Courts EC2 in private sub-networks without any route to the internet need to be managed by Systems Manager (The security policy bans NAT Gateway and any way out to the internet. How to enable the communication of instances with the Systems Manager?
options: Use Gateway VPC Endpoint for the Systems Manager
Install Agent SSM with permanent offline mode
Add one Internet Gateway only for the traffic of SSM
Create interface VPC PrivateLink for the services of the Systems Manager the VPC
saa-med-029.explanation: Interface endpoints expose the APIs of SSM within the VPC with private IPs: the agent of the instances communicates with the service entirely through the network of AWS, without internet NAT.
saa-med-029.hint: Without internet, APIs need to 'enter' VPC — what kind of endpoint creates private interfaces for services such as the SSM?
optionRationales: Interface endpoints expose the APIs of SSM within the VPC with private IPs: the agent of the instances communicates with the service entirely through the network of AWS, without internet NAT.
Internet Gateway it is precisely the route to the public internet that the policy prohibits.
There is no management per 'offline' agent — the SSM requires communication with your endpoints to receive commands and report status.
Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB; for the SSM, the endpoints are interface type (PrivateLink)).

saa-med-030.text: An application connects to Amazon RDS for MySQL using fixed password saved in configuration file. The security team wants to remove static passwords, allowing the application to authenticate in the bank using temporary tokens issued based on the roll IAM of the court. RDS supports this model?
options: Save the password to a AMI custom
Database authentication via IAM (IAM database authentication)
Use the master user of RDS in all applications
Disable bank authentication for internal connections
saa-med-030.explanation: With authentication IAM enabled, the application generates ephemeral tokens (15 minutes) signed from your credentials IAM and use them instead of password — removing static secrets in code and configuration.
saa-med-030.hint: Instead of password saved, a 'ticket of 15 minutes' signed by identity IAM Application.
optionRationales: With authentication IAM enabled, the application generates ephemeral tokens (15 minutes) signed from your credentials IAM and use them instead of password — removing static secrets in code and configuration.
Embed password in image only changes the place of static secret — anyone with access to AMI o obtain.
Bank without authentication is a critical vulnerability, not a security solution.
Sharing the master user concentrates maximum privileges on all components — the opposite of the lowest privilege, and still with static password.

saa-med-031.text: The security team wants to be alerted in minutes if someone logs in with the root user of any organization account. What combination of services implements this alert automatically?
options: Configure the AWS WAF to block root logins
CloudTrail recording the login events and a rule of Amazon EventBridge filtering the root login event to notify via SNS
Enable S3 Block Public Access in the management account
Manually review the credentials report IAM every week
saa-med-031.explanation: The root login console event arrives via CloudTrail/EventBridge; a standard rule for userIdentity root publishes in a topic SNS, alerting the team in near real time.
saa-med-031.hint: The login becomes a EVENTO registered — which double captures the event and triggers notification?
optionRationales: The root login console event arrives via CloudTrail/EventBridge; a standard rule for userIdentity root publishes in a topic SNS, alerting the team in near real time.
The credible report shows the status of credentials, and the weekly review does not meet the warning requirement in minutes.
The WAF filter customer web application traffic — does not intercept or monitor logins on the console of AWS.
Block Public Access protects buckets against public exposure — no relationship with root login monitoring.

saa-med-032.text: An organization wants to structure its accounts into organizational units by separating production, development and security, with the justification of reducing the 'blast radius' of incidents. What security benefit this separation in multiple accounts offers?
options: Multiple accounts eliminate the need for IAM within each
A AWS offers billing discount for organizations with more accounts
Separate accounts automatically fold service limits at no cost
Each account is a rigid border of isolation: a commitment or error in an account does not directly affect the resources of others
saa-med-032.explanation: The account is the strongest insulation limit of the AWS — separate environments and functions in separate accounts contains incidents, simplifies the least privilege and allows guards (SCPs) specific by group.
saa-med-032.hint: Think of compartments of a ship's ponds: hole in one does not flood the others.
optionRationales: The account is the strongest insulation limit of the AWS — separate environments and functions in separate accounts contains incidents, simplifies the least privilege and allows guards (SCPs) specific by group.
The IAM remains essential in each account — separation adds an insulation layer, does not replace internal access control.
Although each account has its own shares, this is an operational effect — not the security benefit that drives the separation.
There is no discount by amount of accounts; consolidated billing adds use, but the argument here is safety insulation.

saa-med-033.text: A serverless application uses functions Lambda who need to read a API Today the credentials are in environment variable in clear text, visible to anyone with reading access to the function configuration. Which safer approach is recommended?
options: Share credentials on a private team channel
Store ID no AWS Secrets Manager and do the function to fetch it in runtime via permissions IAM of execution roll
Save the credentials to the source code to remove them from the configuration
Overshadow the Base64 credentials in the environment variable
saa-med-033.explanation: With the secret Secrets Manager, the function recovers it dynamically with minimal permissions, the value exits the visible configuration, becomes encrypted, auditable and rotateable centrally.
saa-med-033.hint: The secret should live in an auditable safe and be searched only when using — not traveling in clear text in the configuration.
optionRationales: With the secret Secrets Manager, the function recovers it dynamically with minimal permissions, the value exits the visible configuration, becomes encrypted, auditable and rotateable centrally.
Base64 is reversible encoding, not encryption — anyone decodes in seconds.
Secrets in the code leak into repositories and become visible to everyone with access to the source — one of the most classic security errors.
Distributing secrets by communication channels multiplies uncontrollable copies and does not resolve secure storage in execution.

saa-med-034.text: During an audit, it was found that the root user of an account has active key accesses created years ago. AWS, what should be done with these keys?
options: Keep them as backup for emergencies
Share them only with the senior infrastructure team
Exclude them immediately: root should not have programmatic access keys, and administrative tasks should use identities IAM with less privilege
Rotate them monthly and keep them in use
saa-med-034.explanation: Access keys from root are unlimited power credentials, impossible to restrict by policies; the recommendation is to eliminate them and perform the work via roles and users IAM appropriate.
saa-med-034.hint: For the identity that cannot be limited, the only safe programmatic key is the one that does not exist.
optionRationales: Access keys from root are unlimited power credentials, impossible to restrict by policies; the recommendation is to eliminate them and perform the work via roles and users IAM appropriate.
Root 'reservation' keys are a permanent liability: if they leak, they deliver the entire account — the root's emergency access is by password with MFA.
Rotation reduces the exposure window, but does not change the central problem: no automation should operate with unlimited root power.
Restricting the public does not correct the misuse of program root credentials — they simply should not exist.

saa-med-035.text: A fintech needs to restrict access to the console AWS of its administrators to work only from the office's IPs and require MFA in any sensitive action. IAM allows these contextual requirements to be imposed?
options: The Policy Condition element, using keys like aws:SourceIp and aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent
The Resource element with the office IP list
One Security Group attached to console users
User location tags IAM
saa-med-035.explanation: The Condition block assesses the context of the request: conditions with aws:SourceIp restriction by IP band and aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent requires authenticated session with MFA — permissions depending on the circumstances.
saa-med-035.hint: Permissions 'with SE' (if it comes from IP X, if you have MFA) live in the block of political conditions.
optionRationales: The Condition block assesses the context of the request: conditions with aws:SourceIp restriction by IP band and aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent requires authenticated session with MFA — permissions depending on the circumstances.
Resource identifies RNAs of policy target resources — does not accept IP addresses or authentication context.
Tags on identities serve the organization and controls ABAC based on own attributes — do not check the IP of origin or the use of MFA in the sitting.
Security Groups protect network resources (instances, ENIs) — do not apply to user logins on the console.

saa-med-036.text: A company has published a API REST no Amazon API Gateway and wants to prevent it from being called by unauthorized systems, validating in each request a token JWT issued in the users' login by Amazon Cognito. What's the use of API Gateway implements this validation in a managed way?
options: Hide URL of API and not document it.
An Authorizer of the Cognito (Cognito User Pool Authorizer) configured in the methods of API
Place the API behind the Route 53 with weighted rotation
Increase Throttling from API to make external calls difficult
saa-med-036.explanation: The User Pool Authorizer automatically validates or JWT sent to the header against the configured pool, rejecting requests without valid token before reaching the backend — without own validation code.
saa-med-036.hint: The native 'porter' of API Gateway knows how to check badges JWT issued by the user pool.
optionRationales: The User Pool Authorizer automatically validates or JWT sent to the header against the configured pool, rejecting requests without valid token before reaching the backend — without own validation code.
Tax limits control volume, non-identity — unauthorized calls would continue to pass, only slower.
URLs leak into traffic and tools — darkness does not replace authentication.
Policy DNS distributes traffic between endpoints — does not validate tokens or authentic calls.
